### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**62** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `responseSchema (6 routes)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **214** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **154** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **154**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **99** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **184** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b49d9e09c0675e072da7b4a6c812b25d790c0bcf` — the merge of head `a638fafb6631b57bf9d5c44457be95eb57bd7361` into base `cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b49d9e09c0675e072da7b4a6c812b25d790c0bcf && git checkout b49d9e09c0675e072da7b4a6c812b25d790c0bcf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c a638fafb6631b57bf9d5c44457be95eb57bd7361 && git checkout -B drift-repro cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c && git merge --no-ff a638fafb6631b57bf9d5c44457be95eb57bd7361

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a638fafb6631b57bf9d5c44457be95eb57bd7361`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts, packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-served-overrides.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts, packages/core/src/utils/metadata-activation-store.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/rest/src/query-allowlist.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, the two suites (`packages-customizations.test.ts`, `metadata-activation-store.test.ts`), the five `packages/spec/*/api.json` shards, `content/docs/references/**`, the strictness-ledger counts and `.changeset/28411-package-customizations-read.md`

Reviewed against card #28411 (ADR-0146 D8 item 4, D2, D3, D6; epic #28236 child N-15), the seat's order, claim `6553738437` with its amendment `6553788930`, the dev report `6554925948`, and the merged N-10 predicate (PR #28507). Face: `record-recognisers --paths` on the PR's 19 files names the schema face only (`hits` = the one spec path); no declaration or rules face is owed beside it. Read-only: the diff (`origin/main...a638fafb`), the cited code at the head, and the head's check-runs; nothing built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **New published schemas** `GetPackageCustomizationsRequestSchema` and `GetPackageCustomizationsResponseSchema`, with `GetPackageCustomizationsRequest` / `GetPackageCustomizationsResponse` and their `Parsed` types, in `@objectstack/spec/api` beside the other package-route schemas — **correct**, Clause-② widening as declared. Both are `lazySchema` like their siblings; the response is `.strict()` at every level (top, `overrides[]` item, `extensions[]` item, `switchedOff[]` item, `counts`), the counts `z.number().int().nonnegative()`, `extensions[].kind` a closed enum. Nothing the door serves is outside the declaration: the overrides entry is built from conditional spreads (`member`, `basedOn`, `version` only when present; `version` filtered to a non-negative integer), the extensions entry carries `name` only for a named member and `fields` only for an index, `switchedOff` carries `{ type, name }`, and `counts` are the three lengths of the same answer. The fixture case and the extensions case parse the real payload through the response schema. A validation rule without a string name is skipped rather than listed name-less; `ValidationRuleSchema` requires `name`, so no declared extension reaches that branch.
2. **Request schema `{ packageId }` strict vs. the door's closed query set** — **consistent**. The door honours the declaration through `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage(query, [])` (the `@objectstack/rest` helper this domain's other closed doors use) answered `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the parameter, pinned by the suite; the schema is not parsed by code, which is the standing shape of this domain's GET rows (`ListInstalledPackagesRequestSchema` is likewise a declaration the door honours rather than parses).
3. **Route-ledger row** `GET /packages/:id/customizations` (`disposition: 'sdk'`, `client: 'packages.customizations'`, `responseSchema: 'GetPackageCustomizationsResponseSchema'`, no `requestSchema`) — **correct**: none of the other 43 GET rows sets `requestSchema` (the field names a JSON body), so the omission is the ledger's own convention; the census count moves 114 → 115 for the one row; the suite pins `responseSchema` and `client`.
4. **SDK** `client.packages.customizations(id)` — **correct**: `getRoute('packages')` plus `encodeURIComponent(id)/customizations`, unwrapped as `GetPackageCustomizationsResponse`, the shape of `packages.export` beside it.
5. **Runtime door** (`packages.ts`): the order is read gate → closed query set → `.custom` shape refusal → registry lookup → protocol → `readPackageCustomizations` — **correct against the ruling**: `requireReadCapability(deps, _context)` is the same function `GET /packages/:id` calls, asked first, no second authority check; the 404 is `registry.getPackage(id)` with the identical literal `Package '${id}' not found` (the suite compares the two bodies); the `.custom` refusal uses `customizationBasePackageId` from `@objectstack/spec/kernel` (the one suffix spelling) and `deps.error(message, 400, { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' })`, the spelling this file already uses at its closed-query helper, with `HttpDispatcher.error` promoting `details.code`; a failed read answers through `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 500)` like every sibling. No per-organization axis. Nothing in the path creates the pair (no `ensureCustomizationPackage` call; the no-pair case asserts the package count).
6. **Overrides use only N-10's predicate** — **holds**. `protocol-served-overrides.ts` selects the pair's `state: 'active'` rows through `findEnvironmentRows` (environment rows only, system context), keeps each row exactly when `isServedOverrideRowOf(row, base)` holds, folds the type to the canonical singular, drops rows `declinesStoredRow` declines, and dedupes a pre-#4432 spelling pair keeping the canonical row. No body-only `overrides.package === X` spelling exists anywhere in the diff. Read failures go through `rethrowUnlessMetadataStoreUnprovisioned` (falls through to `[]` only for the unprovisioned case). The agreement case checks every listed override against `getMetaItemLayered`'s `overlay` and `effective`.
7. **Extensions**: `getAllObjects(pair)` (objects the pair contributes to) → `getObjectOwner(name).packageId === base` → contributors with `packageId === pair && ownership === 'extend'`, members read from `contributor.definition` — **correct**: `ObjectContributor.definition` is the body as registered and an `extend` body is not planned (#24314), so `fields` / `validations` / `indexes` are the added members, no diff needed; the dependent-package and other-object controls pin the two exclusions.
8. **Switched off**: `listPackageMetadataActivations(ql, base)` filtered to `active === false` — **correct**; a composition without the ledger object answers `[]` (ADR-0126 §4).
9. **Core store refactor** — `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore.list()` is **byte-identical in effect**: the lifted `readActivationLedgerRows` issues the same `find` (`where: { metadata_type }`, `context: SYSTEM_CTX`), the same `name` guard, the same absent-`packageId` spelling and the same `=== false || === 0` read; `list()` strips `metadataType` by destructuring, so each row is `{ name, packageId?, active }` in the original key order. The diff touches no writer (`setActive` and the rest are outside both hunks); the new export guards an empty or non-string package (never the package-less rows). The three new core cases pin this (including the parse-agreement case between the per-package read and the per-type store).
10. **Metadata-protocol surface**: public verb `listServedOverrides({ packageId })` on `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (host-split like `protocol-environment-rows.ts`, the class keeps the signature) and `export type { ServedOverrideEntry }` from the index — **named truthfully** on the `Metadata-protocol: added` line of the changeset body. `PackagesDomainProtocol` types the optional verb off the producer's signature.
11. **Merge of main (#28527, #28512)**: both merge commits are ancestors of the merge-base; `origin/main...a638fafb` touches only the PR's 19 files, and its deletions are the core refactor (22), the census number (1) and the regenerated docs/counts (2 + 5 + 1) — **none of their hunks is edited**. The one conflict (`package-lifecycle.zod.ts`) resolved with both schema blocks kept.
12. **Generated artifacts** — **match the head's source by count and content**: `api-surface` +6 (2 consts, 4 types), `authorable-surface` +6 (the request's `packageId` and the response's five top-level keys), `declaration-map` +4, `export-origins` +6 pointing at `src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts`, `json-schema.manifest` +2, `references/index.mdx` 1580 → 1582 (api 456 → 458), the reference page's tables transcribe the `describe` texts, and the strictness-ledger count 466 → 472 is the six new `z.object` sites (one request, five response). On the head, `Type Check · source gates` (export-origins, authorable-surface, docs) and `Spec property liveness` (strictness ledger) are green; `Type Check · consumer gates` (api-surface) was still in progress when this record was written.

### ② Semver level

Changeset grades `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` **minor** and `@objectstack/core` **patch**, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset — **consistent** with AGENTS.md's rule (a kind takes at least minor on the package the diff moves; the authorable-surface shard moved, so spec is `added` at minor, as the order prescribed; the new verb and type make metadata-protocol minor; the route and the SDK method widen runtime and client) and with the seat's amendment `6553788930`, which fixed core at patch (a non-protocol widening ships patch per AGENTS.md §3). `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no login note owed.
- `open_questions: []` in the dev report; no `needs_decision`.
- **Ablation measured otherwise than the order expected** — **sound**. The read selects the pair's rows by `package_id` (and `state`) before the predicate runs, so a non-pair row never reaches it in either version; of the predicate's three legs only the declaration and the overridable-type legs can discriminate after that selection, and the body-only replacement reds the permission-set control (`OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION`: `permission` is security-catalog, not overridable). The non-pair control stays as a behavioural pin. Disclosed in the PR body; accepted.
- **File surface beyond the claim** (`packages/core`, the new `packages/metadata-protocol` module) — covered by the seat's amendment; neither path is governed.
- **A declared pair row for a name the base does not ship is still listed** — correct reading of the predicate (it does not ask what the base ships) and of ADR-0146 D2 (the publish gate, N-09, owns that refusal); the layered read serves the same row, so the agreement holds. Not pinned by a case here; no action owed on this card.
- **Flow overrides** are excluded via `declinesStoredRow` (a stored row under a shipped flow name) until N-11 arms D9 — the right exclusion, since such a row overrides nothing yet.
- **Not here** honoured: no UI (N-24), no badge or filter (N-19), no restore (N-17), no diff and no `basedOn` verdict (`basedOn` copied as recorded).
- Check-runs on the head: every completed run is green (`Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` and the rest); `Build Core`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace / debt ledger / consumer gates` and the UI shards were still in progress at write time. Landing waits on the full green per the standing rule; this verdict does not.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/package-lifecycle.zod.ts` against ADR-0146 D8 item 4 and its first consumer, the runtime door (and, through it, the landing's counts N-24 and Studio's filter N-19):

- The declaration is the contract of a new route, not a transcription, and it says so in its docblock. It carries D8 item 4 whole: three lists of served rows and ledger rows, "nothing computed from them but the counts", and D2/D6's refusal of a diff or a `basedOn` verdict is written into the `basedOn` member's describe text ("copied as stored and never judged"). The D3 landing line ("n customized, m switched off") is answerable from `counts` without a second read.
- Strict at every level is the right posture for an AI-authored consumer: a member the door starts serving is a schema change first, and the suite parses the real payload, so the declaration and the served shape cannot drift silently. `kind` closed to `field | validation | index` means a new member class is declared before it is served.
- `member` on an override entry is what makes a bundle type (`email_template`, keyed `(name, locale)`) listable without ambiguity, matching how the ledger and `ListPackageCommitsResponse` tell such items apart.
- The request schema's strict `{ packageId }` documents the closed query set; the door enforces it with the shared helper and the refusal names the parameter, so the declaration is honoured, not merely stated.
- Ordering (type, name, member / object, kind, name / type, name) is declared and implemented, so the landing can render without re-sorting.
- No premature surface: no pagination, no per-organization axis, no `basedOn` comparison, no item bodies — each would be a declaration without a puller at this head.

Held. No must-fix.
